Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA comer Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: //vwvw.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 120 s. 2022 October 10, 2022 HON. JENNIFER AUSTRIA-BARZAGA Mayor City of Dasmarinas, Cavite Dear Hon. Austria-Barzaga: This pertains to your letter dated 13 September 2022 addressed to Dir. Ariel O. Iglesia of DILG Regional Office IV-A requesting for the Department's guidance on the payment of compensation of SK Federation President on maternity leave and the Acting SK Federation President during the latter's leave of absence. In your request, these antecedent facts were provided: I. During the leave of absence of the SK Federation President, Hon. Justine Mhae Quillao, an Acting SK Federation President was elected and assumed the ex- officio position of the SK Federation President in the Sanggunian Panglungsod. 2; There was no mention of the reason for the leave of absence of the duly elected SK Federation President. However, in view of the correlation of the query to that of the Expanded Maternity Law, it may be prudent to presume the reason being a maternity leave. The crux of the matter submitted for the Department's comments is with respect to the CSC Opinion on the eligibility of Hon. Quillao to enjoy the benefits of Republic-Act No. 11210 or the Expanded Maternity Law, and the need to remunerate Hon. Trangcoso on her assumption of duty in lieu of Hon. Quillao to the City Sanggunian. The query is whether the payment of both amount to a case of double compensation or if it is a reasonable way to address the situation. We resolve the issue in favor of the legislative intent behind the Expanded Maternity Leave Law, thereby ruling out the existence of double compensation. Foremost, Section 4 of R.A. No. 11210, otherwise known as the Expanded Maternity Leave Law, included in its coverage any pregnant female worker in the government service, regardless of employment status, in Local Government Units (LGUs), among others. To wit: "Section 4. Maternity Leave for Female Workers in the Public Sector.— Any pregnant female worker in the government service, regardless of employment status, in National Government Agencies (NGAs), Local Government Units (LGUs), Government-Owned or -Controlled "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

Corporations (GOCCs), or State Universities and Colleges (SUCs), shall be granted a maternity leave of one hundred five (105) days with full pay regardless if the delivery was normal or caesarian: Provided, That, in case the employee qualifies as a solo parent under Republic Act Nb. 8972, or the "Solo Parents' Welfare Act", the employee shall be paid an additional maternity benefit of fifteen (15) days. An additional maternity leave of thirty (30) days, without pay, can be availed of, at the option of the female worker: Provided, further, That, the head of the agency shall be given due notice, in writing, at least forty-five (45) days before the end of her maternity leave: Provided, finally, That no prior notice shall be necessary in the event of a medical emergency but subsequent notice shall be given to the head of the agency. Maternity leave of sixty (60) days, with full pay, shall be granted fcr miscarriage or emergency termination of pregnancy." The DBM Guidelines on the Compensation and Benefits of Barangay Officialsl provides as follows: "The Liga ng mga Barangay President and the SK Federation President can receive both the fixed salary as ex-officio Sanggunian member from the municipality or city and honorarium from the baranqay at Pl ,000 and P600 per month respectively pursuant to LBC No. 66 and 66A. However, they may only receive the cash gift from only one source. In the event that other officials are validly designated to perform the functions of the Liga President and the SK Federation President in the barangay, the designated officials shall be entitled to collect reimbursable travelling and incidental expenses not exceeding P 1,000 and P600 per month, respectively. The designated officials shall not be entitled to cash gift/christmas bonus." As to the payment of honorarium, the Department has been consistent with the position that an official is not entitled to honorarium in the absence of the required actual services rendered. This is consistent with DILG Opinion No. 124 s. 2010 and DILG Opinion No. 16 s. 2007. We opine, therefore, that the Expanded Maternity Leave Law which authorizes paid maternity leave applies to the payment of the Liga ng mga Barangay President's and SK Federation President's salary as ex-officio member in the Sanggunian. That is in view of the position being a salaried position. However, the same shall not extend to the position as barangay official as there is no corresponding salary therefor and that they instead receive honorarium in recognition of actual services rendered Based on the foregoing, it can be deduced that Hon. Quillao, the SK Federation President who is on maternity leave, is entitled only to the fixed salary as ex-officio member of the sanggunian panlungsod. She is not entitled to the honorarium from her position in the barangay as SK official as no actual service was rendered from her end. 1 https://www.dbm.gov.ph/wp-content/upIoads/2012/03/BB-5.pdf Page 2 of 3

With respect to Hon. Trangcoso, the Acting SK Federation President, she is entitled to collect reimbursable travelling and incidental expenses not exceeding Pl ,000 and P600 per month, respectively. She is not entitled to the salary of an ex-officio member of the sanggunian. She is likewise entitled to honorarium with respect to the actual services rendered in the barangay as SK official. We hope to have enlightened you on the matter. Very truly yours, BY AUTH RITY OF THE SEC ICT R LLAMAS A TY.
